verdict.rationale: Many irs.gov guidance pages yielded verbatim quoted content to the pipeline: the EIN page, SS-4 filing addresses, the MeF overview, the e-file provider page, IRIS, the account-creation page, the Pub 525 update and mobile-friendly forms. That indicates the public reading surface serves server-rendered text without a bot wall or CAPTCHA. The content host also returns ordinary 404s rather than challenge pages. The only 403 observed was the signed Form 15620 application flow, which sits behind sign-in and is not part of the guidance reading surface. Missing for 10: an explicit probe recording HTTP 200 on a guidance page with an identified user agent, the robots.txt policy for the www.irs.gov content host, and direct confirmation that the pages are not JS-dependent.
